messages:
leah_sales: quick sync from the kickoff: Swivel asked for a migration-proof POC that behaves like their API. they want to validate request/response parity + perf. capturing action items here.

omar_se: can someone paste the canonical Swivel request/response examples they sent? need to map fields and function-calling differences.

leah_sales: pasted from their tech lead:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"model\": \"swivel-2x\",
  \"prompt\": \"Extract key decisions from notes:\",
  \"conversation_id\": \"sess_123\",
  \"max_tokens\": 300
}
```
Response body: `outputs: [{ text: ..., metadata: {...} }]`. they assert side-effect on conversation state inside the same call (so server holds session).

omar_se: Redwood uses `choices` with `message` objects and explicit `conversation_id` carried in request/response metadata. notable diffs to validate:
- envelope: outputs[] vs choices[].message
- tool calls: their tool_call object is single, ours is `tool_calls` array with richer schema
- streaming semantics: they stream whole chunks less frequently, ours streams delta tokens aggressively

mike_sre: operationally, Swivel pins session cache to instance which gives warm state assumptions. our default multi-tenant pooling evicts faster. for parity we can run Dedicated with pinned caches but need to size memory and pick GPU SKUs. target perf they quoted: p99 < 350ms at 512 tokens.

simon_infra: i'll draft infra plan: rg name, instance types (A100-80GB vs H100), expected batch sizes, and how we measure p99. will include mem + KV cache warmup instructions.

nina_security: enterprise checklist: VPC peering, BYOK/KMS, 12mo audit log retention (they asked 1y), IP allowlists, datacenter residency EU. do we have current SOC2 + recent pentest summary? legal will want non-prod data retention terms and ability to opt-out of caching per-request.

ray_customer: to confirm: we need per-prompt opt-out and explicit cache-disable flag for sensitive prompts. also need proof we can rotate keys without downtime (JWK rotation) and HSM support for Private deployments.

omar_se: parity gotcha: tokenizers. they use a UTF-8 byte-level tokenizer, ours is slightly different which moves stop tokens and can cause extra tokens or truncated results. plan: run a small harness comparing encoded lengths and stops on the 50-prompt suite. recommend adding explicit stop tokens in prompts to reduce divergence.

leah_sales: procurement questions surfaced: are committed discounts transferable to Dedicated? how do we charge for prefix cache tokens and embeddings? they want a TCO estimate for 100M generation tokens + 10M embeddings/month.

simon_infra: short: Dedicated is separate pricing (reserved monthly) — committed credits for hosted don't map 1:1. prefix cache isn't billed separately as tokens but increases inference compute; we'll provide example cost breakdown. embeddings billed per vector; we can simulate with sample throughput.

omar_se: function-calling parity: Swivel's tool args are ordered arrays (clients rely on that sequence). Redwood sometimes emits object maps (unordered). quick mitigation: provide a compatibility adapter that converts our tool_calls into their ordered args shape for the POC layer. will prototype. note: add latency telemetry for the shim.

leah_sales: dev-bot created env: rg-poc-swivel-2026, creds shared in 1:1.

dev-bot: POC workspace and a metrics dashboard stub live at https://console.redwood/poc/rg-poc-swivel-2026

ray_customer: can you run the 50-prompt suite and return divergence rates (metrics: rouge, emd, exact-match). we'll flag anything > 5% divergence for follow-up.

omar_se: yes. i'll run against our tuned quantized build and Swivel's sample endpoint, will post a summary table here by Tue EOD.

nina_security: blocker: SOC2 report and pentest. we can provide compensating controls (limited retention, read-only log exports) during POC but legal will still request the formal reports.

simon_infra: action list I will deliver: infra runbook + perf target tests + cost delta for pinned-cache config (due Tue EOD).

omar_se: I'll deliver parity eval + tokenizer diff analysis + shim prototype (due Tue EOD).

nina_security: I'll assemble security packet, confirm BYOK/HSM options for Private, and JWK rotation process (due Wed).

leah_sales: i'll update commercial terms draft (caching clauses, retention, discount mapping) and schedule the legal pre-call after metrics land.

Any immediate blockers? :eyes: 

ray_customer: main blocker is SOC2 + pentest timeline. otherwise good to proceed.

leah_sales: thanks team 44d i'll post call notes + the 50-prompt suite attachment after this thread.
